transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-18
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Zenno Head of ML), Ethan Moore (Platform Eng), Sofia Diaz (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Zenno is exploring Redwood's self-serve hosted API to get to first token quickly; evaluating tradeoffs for Dedicated / Private given PII campaign data and latency SLAs. They want clear quickstart steps, free credits, and a small bench to validate cost/latency. Action items: share quickstart + security docs, provision credits, run short bench.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya from redwood, i handle the account here. quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya (Zenno): hey i'm priya kapoor, head of ml at zenno, and i'm primarily focused on how fast we can get a model into our email personalization pipeline.
[00:16] Ethan (Zenno): ethan here, platform eng. i'll own infra questions and network/security.
[00:19] Sofia (Zenno): sofia, product, i'll be the PM working with priya.
[00:23] Liam (Redwood): liam, solution engineer, will do the technical walkthrough and help with quickstart runbook.
[00:27] Maya (Redwood): awesome. today's goal: show how to get to first token with our hosted API, review when you'd want dedicated or private, and agree next steps.

[01:02] Priya (Zenno): high level context — zenno runs personalized email campaigns at scale, some datasets are PII and we need controls. latency target is sub-150ms for scoring, and cost matters bc we do millions of tokens a month. we want to evaluate self-serve first.

[02:10] Liam (Redwood): great. self-serve hosted is fastest to test: you can sign up, get free credits, and hit the API via SDK or curl. typical time-to-first-token for teams is under 20 minutes if you have a prompt ready. we'll show a tiny demo.

[03:05] Ethan (Zenno): quick Q: the free credits — are they per-account or per-seat, and do they expire?
[03:12] Maya (Redwood): typically promo credits we add to the org account and they expire in 30 days by default — we'll provision 60 USD worth for you to experiment; let us know if you want a different amount, we can escalate.

[04:00] Liam (Redwood): demo plan: 1) quick signup, 2) api key issuance, 3) run a curl text-generation, 4) show SDK snippet and streaming, 5) show console usage and billing meter. i'll also outline dedicated/private criteria.

[05:15] (screen-sharing starts, audio descriptions omitted)
[05:40] Liam (Redwood): here's the quick curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","prompt":"subject: welcome to zenno"}' — that returns a tokenized response. note: exact path may vary in the UI, typos in sample snippets are common in transcripts.

[07:05] Sofia (Zenno): okay so that's basically it — get key and fire off a call. any SDKs? we use node and python.
[07:12] Liam (Redwood): yes, official SDKs for python/node. node example: import Redwood from '@redwoodai/client'; const c = new Redwood({apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY}); await c.generate(...). we also have a cli for quick local tests.

[08:30] Priya (Zenno): about dedicated vs hosted — what metrics should we look at to decide? our campaigns ramp seasonally and sometimes need bursty throughput.

[09:01] Liam (Redwood): good question. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools — predictable throughput and isolation, and you can configure autoscaling/burst. hosted is multitenant but cost-efficient for lower or variable usage. usually decision factors: monthly token volume, SLOs (p95 latency), data residency/compliance, and whether you need private control plane.

[10:23] Ethan (Zenno): security: we need SOC2, SSO, audit logs, and a way to bring our own KMS for encryption keys. also VPC peering for private deployments — what do you support?

[10:38] Maya (Redwood): we have SOC2 reports and an enterprise security pack. for Private, we support customer VPC and on-prem options; KMS integrations and HSM for keying are available under Private. SSO/SAML and RBAC are available on Dedicated/Private; hosted supports org-level SSO with SCIM for user provisioning. we'll share the security packet after this call.

[12:05] Priya (Zenno): if we start with hosted to iterate, how do we later migrate to Dedicated or Private? is there vendor lock-in or big migration work?

[12:22] Liam (Redwood): we built an abstraction to make that smooth: same API surface, you can pin model versions and change routing policies. migration typically requires network setup for Private and config changes, but your prompts and code usually remain the same. small note — sometimes kernel/quantization differences can affect latency/cost slightly, so we recommend a short benchmark.

[14:00] Priya (Zenno): benchmark — can you give us an example bench for our workload? we do short prompts (<=128 tokens) with KV-style caching patterns in front.

[14:18] Liam (Redwood): yes — we can provide a notebook that runs payloads against hosted and a simulated dedicated config so you can compare p95 latency and tokens per second. we'll include batching and KV cache emulation (we call it KV cash in non-native transcripts).

[15:45] Ethan (Zenno): cost controls — we want per-route cost attribution and token-level breakdowns. does Redwood Console show that?
[15:53] Maya (Redwood): console shows token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and you can set quotas and rate limits. for Dedicated you also get reserved capacity billing.

[17:07] Sofia (Zenno): are there built-in evals or quality monitoring? we need regressions alerts linked to prompt sets.

[17:16] Liam (Redwood): yes, Redwood Optimize includes evals for prompt sets, quality monitors, and automatic regression alerts. we can hook your golden prompts in and alert on drift.

[19:00] Priya (Zenno): can we test streaming responses? we use streaming for progressive UI updates.

[19:08] Liam (Redwood): streaming supported via SDK and server-sent events, and function/tool calling is supported for structured JSON outputs. we'll demo streaming in the hands-on.

[21:02] Ethan (Zenno): network egress concerns — if we do hosted, is data stored? how long do you keep logs, can we opt out?

[21:15] Maya (Redwood): hosted has default logging/retention but we offer data retention controls; for strict no-retention you'd look at Private. we can also configure masking or redaction. we'll include retention options in the security packet.

[23:00] Priya (Zenno): timeline: if we like hosted quickstart, we can onboard devs and run a 2-week pilot. if pilot looks good, then plan for Dedicated for seasonality. is that realistic?

[23:12] Liam (Redwood): absolutely. typical pattern: pilot on hosted, then commit to Dedicated when you hit predictable volume or need SSO+SLA. we can help with canary rollouts and A/B traffic splits when migrating.

[25:00] Sofia (Zenno): any gotchas about accuracy/regressions between hosted and dedicated model variants? we saw differences with other vendors.

[25:10] Liam (Redwood): small differences can appear due to quantization or model variant; Redwood maintains a model catalog with verified perf profiles to reduce surprises. we also recommend prompt-level regression tests in Redwood Optimize.

[27:00] (short pause)
[27:12] Maya (Redwood): next i'll go over the quickstart checklist verbally so you can see time-to-first-token flow.

[27:20] Maya (Redwood): step 1: sign up as org admin, step 2: verify org, step 3: get API key (1-2 min), step 4: run example curl/SDK (under 5 min), step 5: add sample dataset to bench. we can provision org credits immediately and Liam will help with the notebook.

[29:05] Ethan (Zenno): what about rate limits? we need burst capacity for send windows.

[29:12] Liam (Redwood): hosted has tiered rate limits; Dedicated gives predictable throughput via GPU pools and you can configure burst windows. we can also enable caching to reduce per-token volume during bursts.

[30:30] Priya (Zenno): do you support bring-your-own-model where we host a customer model?

[30:40] Liam (Redwood): on Private you can bring your own model or containerize a model and run in your environment; in Dedicated we can host curated models for you. hosted is typically Redwood-managed open models or vetted variants.

[32:05] Sofia (Zenno): legal/procurement: any standard terms for PII? how do we engage legal?

[32:20] Maya (Redwood): we'll share a starter SOW and our enterprise terms. procurement usually starts after pilot if Dedicated/Private is selected. for PII workflows we have addendum language; we'll loop in legal after you review the security pack.

[34:00] Priya (Zenno): small nit: in the sample curl you showed the model name — is there a catalog and perf numbers per model?

[34:12] Liam (Redwood): yes, model catalog in the console shows latency and cost profiles, recommended quantization per workload, and verified benchmarks. it's curated and we update it as models evolve.

[35:50] Maya (Redwood): recap: we'll provision $60 credits; send quickstart link, security packet, and a benchmark notebook. liam will run the hands-on bench with your sample dataset.

[36:05] Priya (Zenno): that sounds good. can we get the bench results before our sprint planning next tuesday?

[36:12] Liam (Redwood): we'll aim to run the bench and share results by friday 2025-04-25.

[37:30] Sofia (Zenno): small question about SDK versions — how are updates handled? we want semver and changelogs.

[37:40] Liam (Redwood): yes semver, changelogs in the repo, and we publish release notes. for breaking changes we give migration guides.

[39:00] (some crosstalk, background noise)
[39:20] Ethan (Zenno): ok final ask: can you include an example minimal terraform or cloud run example for integrating the API key securely?

[39:28] Maya (Redwood): yes we'll include a simple terraform example and a recommended best practice for secrets (KMS+env in CI), plus a sample for token rotation.

[40:15] Priya (Zenno): great. thanks team.
[40:18] Maya (Redwood): thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the hands-on.
[40:25] Liam (Redwood): thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript.
